A_general.open_code_note: No official public repository or package for the hosted server was found in the prepared evidence. The separate docs.attio.com/mcp endpoint is a documentation search server and is not the product server analyzed here.
other_official_servers: https://docs.attio.com/mcp is a distinct Attio Docs MCP server. Its manifest describes documentation search and retrieval, a submit_feedback tool, and a documentation skill resource; these are not tools of https://mcp.attio.com/mcp.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Attio says an account on any plan is sufficient and all workspace members can use MCP; no separate MCP fee is listed. The query-particle-sql tool is not available on every billing plan.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing page lists Free at €0 per user/month, Plus at €39 monthly or €31 annual billing per user/month, Pro at €93 monthly or €74 annual billing per user/month, and Enterprise at a custom annual price.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The MCP documentation identifies per-workspace rate limits: Read 100 requests/second; Write 25/second; Merge 5/second; Search 300/minute; Semantic search, Reporting, and SQL 2/second each. Calls in each tier share a workspace bucket. SQL access depends on plan.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires an Attio account, an MCP-compatible AI client, OAuth sign-in, and selection of a workspace during sign-in. An AI-client administrator may need to enable the connector. Client-managed approval settings may restrict which tools can be set to run without approval. SQL is plan-dependent.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Attio controls account permissions, workspace access, MCP rate limits, and plan availability for SQL. The workspace member authorizes the connection. AI-client administrators and users control connector enablement and client-side approval settings.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 without a token and a WWW-Authenticate header pointing to protected-resource metadata. The metadata names https://app.attio.com as authorization server and lists scopes mcp, offline_access, openid. The authorization-server metadata supports authorization_code and refresh_token grants, S256 PKCE, and Dynamic Client Registration at https://app.attio.com/oauth/register. Token endpoint auth methods are none and client_secret_post; bearer tokens are sent in the header. Token lifetime is not stated. Revocation endpoint is https://app.attio.com/oidc/revoke.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tool classes: docs provide rate-limit tiers for reads, writes, merge, search, semantic search, reporting, and SQL; no per-tool safety-annotation values are published. Writes and deletes are present; merge-records merges two records. 2. The help page says clients request confirmation for writes and auto-approve reads; this is client behavior, not a documented server-enforced confirmation parameter or preview flow. 3. OAuth acts as the user's Attio account; documentation says access follows that account's permissions. User sessions can be revoked in Attio settings. No token lifetime, client allowlist, or admin-side Attio switch is documented. 4. No read-only endpoint, tool filter, or environment mode is documented. SQL is read-only by tool description and plan-dependent. 5. Docs say the server operates within the workspace and permissions. No MCP-specific masking or PII exclusion is described. 6. Per-workspace rate tiers: Read 100/s, Write 25/s, Merge 5/s, Search 300/min, Semantic search 2/s, Reporting 2/s, SQL 2/s. No output truncation or per-call price documented. 7. Tool schemas and server-side coercion/correction behavior are not published. 8. Docs claim all operations are logged and auditable; logging implementation and telemetry details are not disclosed. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or upsell tool appears in the complete official product tool list. The query-particle-sql tool is a read-only escape hatch for workspace data. 10. Attio help recommendations include unique identifiers, precise object names, and exact attribute names; these are prompt guidance, not documented server enforcement. No server-delivered skill is documented. 11. No MCP-specific memory or state behavior documented. 12. Flat documented tool list at this endpoint; the separate docs search MCP is a different endpoint. 13. query-particle-sql permits read-only SQL queries; no arbitrary write, script, or raw API tool is listed.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public server code or verbatim tools/list plus initialize instructions were available for the input endpoint; the docs table contains names and summaries only.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The help article explicitly says Attio MCP does not draft or send email; it provides context for the assistant to draft and the user to review/send, or a separate mailbox integration may place a draft. The official tool list contains no email-send tool. No record-delete tool is listed, although the product has a separate archive/delete model and REST API; the MCP list does include delete-comment and delete-task. Sources: https://attio.com/help/reference/how-to-guides/attio-mcp-prompts-and-best-practices, https://docs.attio.com/mcp/overview, https://docs.attio.com/docs/archiving-vs-deleting.md

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Help guidance recommends naming the object, using precise names and unique identifiers, checking exact attribute names/options, and asking the assistant to report changes. It also recommends slowing down or spacing requests after rate-limit errors. These are instructions to the user/client; no matching server enforcement is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Attio states: “Access is tied to your Attio user permissions”; “Attio MCP only operates within your workspace”; “All operations are logged and auditable”; and “Sessions can be revoked from your Attio account settings.” Its privacy policy says it may receive “information relating to your connection between Attio and such third-party services” when services are accessed through an MCP.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The help article says the assistant “can only see and change what your own permissions allow.” It also says the MCP does not draft or send email, and that mailbox-synced sent email appears on the record automatically.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata supports protected access but does not disclose permission enforcement details beyond the official docs. The docs claim workspace/user permission boundaries and auditable operations; the closed hosted implementation cannot be inspected here to verify these claims. Approval before writes is described as client behavior. Rate limits are documented as server-side per-workspace limits.

contradictions: MartechDB reports 42 tools for the official MCP server, while the current official docs enumerate 48. The official changelog documents six activity tools added on 2026-10-14, accounting for the difference. https://martechdb.com/vendors/attio ; https://docs.attio.com/mcp/overview ; https://docs.attio.com/changelog/mcp.md

The OAuth metadata lists general scopes mcp, offline_access, and openid; documentation describes access as following the user's workspace permissions. The metadata does not expose separate read/write scopes, so the precise enforcement relationship is undocumented. https://mcp.attio.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource ; https://app.attio.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server ; https://docs.attio.com/mcp/overview
observations_for_research: OAuth metadata advertises a single MCP scope alongside identity and offline-access scopes; the scopes do not distinguish read from write access.
The documented approval flow relies on AI-client behavior. Attio documents client-side default approval recommendations, while individual server safety annotation values are not published.
The product server offers a read-only SQL tool, but its availability depends on the customer's billing plan.
The docs-search MCP at docs.attio.com has its own search, virtual documentation filesystem, feedback tool, and skill resource; these belong to a separate server surface.
